attrs.management_says: (Implicit) No specific explanation for quarterly receivables pattern.
attrs.numbers_show: Q1–Q3: receivables grew 10–14% vs revenue 5–8%, DSO rose 1–2 days each quarter (E25, E26, E27). Q4: receivables fell 0.3% vs revenue +7%, DSO dropped 39 to 37 (E28). Full-year receivables flat, DSO improved. Pattern suggests intra-year buildup (possible seasonality/channel loading) that reversed by year-end.

attrs.management_says: Core working capital decreased 34% driven by 'continued benefits from our payment terms extension program and lower inventory balances' (E54).
attrs.numbers_show: Receivables were essentially flat (-0.3%, E7, E18) while revenue grew 7.1% (E23), so DSO improved from 39 to 36 days (E23). Quarterly DSO rose in Q1–Q3 (37→38, 33→35, 35→37) then fell sharply in Q4 (39→37) (E25–E28). The 'payment terms extension program' likely refers to extending payables (reducing core working capital), not customer terms, which would increase DSO. The full-year receivables/DSO improvement is consistent with strong collection or mix shift, but the quarterly pattern (build then release) is not explained.

Management's 'payment terms extension program' likely extends payables (reducing core working capital), but does not explain the receivables/DSO improvement or the intra-year build-and-release pattern.
